text:
anya: heads-up: i've been prototyping a tiny local dev agent to issue short-lived tokens for the sampleapp. goal is to remove onboarding friction so users don't need to create k8s secrets for demos. want feedback on env/socket UX.

chris: nice. does it mirror the production sidecar behavior? specifically, socket + file + env fallback?

tay: +1. local dev should be predictable but also close to prod. can you summarize the precedence rules?

anya: precedence is: 1) sidecar socket at $REDWOOD_SOCKET (default /run/redwood/agent.sock) 2) credential file at $REDWOOD_CRED_DIR/creds.json (default /run/redwood/creds) 3) env var named RW_EPHEMERAL_TOKEN (legacy REDWOOD_API_TOKEN honored if present but logged). The SDK helper will try socket first, then file, then env.

kai: question: why RW_EPHEMERAL_TOKEN vs REDWOOD_API_TOKEN? any compatibility requirements?

chris: we should avoid stomping on existing envs. prefer RW_EPHEMERAL_TOKEN to make short-lived nature explicit. but SDKs should read REDWOOD_API_TOKEN as legacy fallback with a warning.

anya: agreed. local agent `redwood dev-agent --ttl 24h` writes to the file and can optionally export the env for interactive shells. demo includes `redwood dev-agent --shell bash` which prints `export RW_EPHEMERAL_TOKEN=...`.

infra-bot: build:dev-agent passed (build 3860) :white_check_mark:

jordan: small UX nit: on macOS with Docker for Mac, /run mounting is flaky. can we allow REDWOOD_CRED_DIR override and document it in the quickstart?

anya: done. sidecar and dev-agent both accept --cred-dir and env override REDWOOD_CRED_DIR. added note for mac users to use /tmp/redwood.

chris: rotation behavior: if the sidecar renews a token, how do running processes pick up the new value? env isn't enough.

tay: yes, env is static per process. recommend libs use a token provider API so they fetch on demand or subscribe to a socket.

anya: exact plan: SDK helper exposes `getToken({preferSocket:true, envName:"RW_EPHEMERAL_TOKEN"})` and a `watchToken(callback)` that uses the socket to push updates when available. examples in JS and Python in the demo repo.

kai: parity ask: make sure py client exposes same method names. in the past we had divergences (get_token vs fetch_token). pick camelCase or snake_case?

chris: follow language idioms: JS -> getToken/watchToken, Python -> get_token/watch_token. keep behavior equivalent and document crosswalk table.

jordan: logging: on renew failures please include control-plane request_id and a stable error code (e.g., ERR_TOKEN_RENEW_401). will help support traces.

anya: will add request_id + ERR_* codes. also emitting metrics: renewal_attempts, renewal_failures{project,node_pool,reason}.

chris: retry policy details? exponential backoff + jitter? cap? when to fallback to long-lived secret?

anya: renewer uses exp backoff with full jitter, base=500ms, cap=30s. after 5 consecutive failures, sidecar tries to read long-lived project token from $REDWOOD_PROJECT_SECRET (k8s secret) and switches to fallback mode and emits metric fallback_engaged=1.

kai: control-plane idempotency: if two nodes call renew at same time, do we get duplicate tokens? that's an operational mess for audits.

anya: control plane accepts an idempotency_key header and will return the existing token if renew happened recently (until TTL-5s). sampleapp will send node_id as idempotency_key by default. documented in the demo notes.

chris: for the SDK helper, what about caching? should it cache token until TTL-10s and then refresh async?

tay: yes, async refresh is nice: return current token immediately and kick off refresh if close to expiry. surface a boolean `stale` or `expires_in`.

anya: implemented in demo helpers: getToken() returns { token, expires_at } in JS (or tuple in python). if expires_in < refresh_threshold (default 15s) helper starts refresh in background.

infra-bot: reminder: demo branch will auto-delete in 7 days unless retention flagged.

jordan: docs: please add a minimal docker-compose example for local dev showing dev-agent + app mounting socket and using helper. that will help new hires.

anya: added docker-compose.yml and a short quickstart in docs. also included troubleshooting: if you see INVALID_ENV_WARNING check for REDWOOD_API_TOKEN set by other tools.

chris: can we run a short walkthrough at the next onboarding session? i'd like to show the socket-based flow vs env fallback.

anya: yes — i'll schedule a 20m demo and push the staging link. staging URL: https://staging.redwood.example/dev-agent (creds in 1password).

kai: LGTM. thanks anya for iterating quickly.

anya: thanks all — will upload the SDK PRs after the demo and add the crosswalk table for method names.

chris: :thumbsup:
